definition: json_schema — the output must parse as JSON, and when `config.schema` is present it must also VALIDATE against that schema. The rule FAILS when JSON.parse throws, or when the parsed value does not satisfy the configured schema. When `config.schema` is absent the rule passes any parseable JSON and says in its message that the shape was not checked — which is exactly the behaviour every already-deployed rule had before 0.11.0, so none of them changes meaning. A schema Iris declines to compile (the guard ladder in src/eval/schema-validator.ts) is a CONFIG ERROR reported at deploy time, not a silent pass. Validation runs through the same hardened validator a tools catalogue goes through: formats are annotations and are not enforced, and the instance is never mutated. Rule: src/eval/rules/custom.ts. Positive = the output should FAIL under the config declared below.
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-05 for arc 4, REWRITTEN rather than extended. The previous family was labelled against a definition that ignored the schema ("passes when the output parses"), so every one of its cases measured a question the type no longer asks. One config is declared here and every case is read against it: two required properties of different types, an optional array of strings, an optional nested object with its own required boolean, and additionalProperties false — which between them exercise required, type, integer-versus-number, array items, nesting and the closed-object clause.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition above on 2026-09-05, by reading each output against the declared config rather than by running the rule. Each note states which clause decided the label. Cases the measurement then disagrees with are reported as errors, not relabelled.
